         Question Paper Finalised Marking Instructions




© Scottish Qualifications Authority 2025

These marking instructions have been prepared by examination teams for use by SQA appointed
markers when marking external course assessments.

The information in this document may be reproduced in support of SQA qualifications only on a non-
commercial basis. If it is reproduced, SQA must be clearly acknowledged as the source. If it is to be
reproduced for any other purpose, written permission must be obtained from permissions@sqa.org.uk.




                                                                                                  ©
General marking principles for National 5 Music

Always apply these general principles. Use them in conjunction with the detailed marking
instructions, which identify the key features required in candidates’ responses.

(a)   Marking should always be positive. This means that, for each candidate response, marks are
      accumulated for the demonstration of relevant skills, knowledge and understanding: they are
      not deducted from a maximum on the basis of errors or omissions.

(b)   If a specific candidate response does not seem to be covered by either the principles or detailed
      marking instructions, and you are uncertain how to assess it, you must seek guidance from your
      team leader.

(c)   Marks for each candidate response must always be assigned in line with these general marking
      principles and the detailed marking instructions for this assessment.

(d)   Where a candidate has provided more than one answer, for example by ticking two boxes
      instead of one or adding an extra wrong answer, place a cross beside the wrong answer and do
      not award the mark assigned to the correct answer.

(e)   Do not accept any answer that is not in the marking instructions. Use professional judgement
      when candidates’ responses do not exactly match marking instructions but carry the same
      meaning, for example pluck/plucked = plucking.

(f)   Candidates are asked to tick one or two boxes in multiple choice questions. Accept a cross or
      any other sign which makes the candidate’s intentions clear.

(g)   Accept inaccurate spelling where the candidate’s intention is clear.

  (b)   (i)     ✓    Rapping                           1     Do not accept other answers here.

        (ii)   The response must include               1     Accept an answer that implies both
                                                             vocals and music, for example:
               • vocals or lyrics or rhyming or
                                                             •   speaking over a beat
                 words
                                                             •   there is singing over hip hop
               and                                           •   talking in song – in this example,
                                                                 song is accepted as a second
               beat or rhythm or music or                        bullet point response as it implies
               accompaniment                                     a piece of music
                                                             •   lyrics with background singing – in
                                                                 this example background singing is
                                                                 accepted as a second bullet point
                                                                 response as background implies
                                                                 accompaniment.

                                                             Do not accept answers such as:

                                                             •   the words are being sung quickly –
                                                                 in this example, the word ‘sung’
                                                                 refers to the vocals and does not
                                                                 imply beat, rhythm, background
                                                                 music, or accompaniment.
                                                             •   it's a person speaking while singing
                                                                 – in this example singing is not
                                                                 accepted as a second bullet point
                                                                 response because it does not
                                                                 imply beat, rhythm, music or
                                                                 accompaniment.

                                                             Rap or rapping should not be
                                                             credited.

                                                             Disregard additional answers.

8.                                             5     • Award 1 mark for each correct
                                                       answer up to a maximum of 2
                                                       concepts per heading and up to a
                                                       total of 5 marks.
                                                     • Do not penalise the candidate if a
                                                       concept appears to be in the wrong
                                                       context for example
                                                       — the tempo is mf or
                                                       — melody/harmony — 4 beats in
                                                         the bar.
                                                     • To achieve full marks, candidate
                                                       must comment at least 3 headings
                                                       — melody/harmony
                                                       — rhythm/tempo
                                                       — instruments
                                                       — dynamics (Italian terms).
                                                     • Answers can be in the form of
                                                       bullet points or short answer or
                                                       sentences or continuous prose and
                                                       any of these are acceptable.
                                                     • Long lists of concepts unrelated to
                                                       the music and/or extensive lists of
                                                       contradictory concepts will result
                                                       in penalties being applied.
                                                     • Accept inaccurate spelling of
                                                       English or Italian terms where the
                                                       candidate has made their
                                                       intentions clear.

           Melody/harmony
           • change of key                                  Also accept modulation.
           • chromatic
           • countermelody
           • glissando                                      Also accept gliss.
           • major
           • perfect cadence
           • repetition *                                   *Accept repetition once only.
           • sequence
           • trill(s)
           Rhythm/tempo
           • 2 or 4 beats in a bar or 2/4 or 4/4
             or simple time
           • accents
           • allegro
           • drum fill(s)
           • repetition *                                   *Accept repetition once only.
           • syncopation or off the beat
           Instruments
           • acoustic or electric guitar                    Do not accept guitar on its own.
           • bass guitar
           • drum kit                                       Do not accept drums.
           • flute or piccolo
           • glockenspiel                                   Also accept glock.
           • saxophone(s)
           • timpani                                        Also accept kettle drum(s).
           • trombone(s)
           • trumpet(s)
           • xylophone                                      Also accept xylo.

           Dynamics (Italian terms)
           • mp or mf                                       Accept Italian terms in full, eg forte.
           • f or ff                                        Do not accept English equivalents.
           • crescendo or cresc. or
           • sforzando or sfz                               No other answers accepted here.
